szoveg_eredeti:
AI Case Discussion and Virtual Consultations Boost Medical Students’ Knowledge

Undergraduate medical students who engaged in artificial intelligence-assisted case discussions and virtual patient consultations achieved significantly higher knowledge scores than peers who learned solely by watching instructional videos, according to research published in BMC Medical Education. The experimental investigation assessed how integrating artificial intelligence tools into clinical training influences student learning outcomes, intrinsic motivation, and professional interaction dimensions.

Although artificial intelligence holds broad application prospects across contemporary medical education, systematic empirical evidence regarding its actual effectiveness in facilitating case discussions and virtual patient consultation has remained scarce. To evaluate these educational technologies systematically, the researchers recruited undergraduate medical students and conducted controlled experiments designed to examine the specific pedagogical effects of artificial intelligence-assisted case discussion and virtual consultation sessions.

A total of 207 medical undergraduates participated in the study using a self-developed intelligent experimental platform. Through this specialized digital environment, the participating medical students engaged directly in artificial intelligence-assisted case discussions and virtual patient consultations, allowing the researchers to measure learning outcomes under structured experimental conditions across two distinct investigation phases.

In Experiment 1, the research team employed a single-factor, three-level between-subjects design to evaluate pedagogical efficacy. This initial experiment compared the effects of artificial intelligence-assisted case discussion, peer case discussion, and a lecture-only control condition. Across these three distinct experimental conditions, the investigators examined and compared the participating medical students’ knowledge acquisition, intrinsic motivation, and interaction quality.

In Experiment 2, the researchers utilized a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design to investigate the effects of virtual patient consultation and the specific sequencing of educational interventions. This experiment analyzed knowledge acquisition, intrinsic motivation, and consultation process quality across several instructional arrangements, including a dedicated virtual consultation group, a consultation-then-discussion group, and a discussion-then-consultation group. Across both experiments, the control group participants were the same individuals.

The experimental results revealed that the artificial intelligence-assisted case discussion group achieved significantly higher knowledge scores than the lecture-only control group. Furthermore, in the second experiment, the virtual consultation group, the consultation-then-discussion group, and the discussion-then-consultation group all outperformed the control condition in knowledge acquisition, confirming that both artificial intelligence-assisted discussion and virtual patient encounters enhanced student learning compared with instructional videos alone.

The findings also revealed that the order of learning activities produced differential effects on clinical performance and engagement. Specifically, the discussion-then-consultation sequence demonstrated higher intrinsic motivation and consultation comprehensiveness, yet exhibited lower empathy than the virtual consultation group. The authors concluded that these results offer theoretical foundations and practical guidance for structuring artificial intelligence-empowered interventions in medical education.

Subject of Research: Pedagogical effects of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual patient consultation in medical education

Article Title: Effects of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual patient consultation on medical students’ learning outcomes

Article References: Gao, H., Zhao, B., Hu, X., Liu, C., Zhang, D., & Zhang, H. (2026). Effects of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual patient consultation on medical students’ learning outcomes. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-10901-8

Keywords: medical education, artificial intelligence, virtual patient consultation, case discussion, knowledge acquisition, intrinsic motivation, empathy, consultation comprehensiveness, interaction quality, undergraduate medical students, instructional videos, peer case discussion, between-subjects design, consultation process quality, intelligent experimental platform, pedagogical effects, intervention sequencing
